newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish 97 pulp, paper exports to rise 7 pct - METLA.
newsitem.headline: Finnish 97 pulp, paper exports to rise 7 pct - METLA.

text.p: Finnish exports of pulp and paper will rise almost seven percent and all forest industry export prices except newsprint will rise slightly, the Finnish Forest Research Institute (METLA) forecast on Wednesday.
Pulp and paper demand would grow as European economic growth would speed up, it said in a statement.
"Unit prices of paper products are forecast to rise five to 10 percent next year," METLA said.
However, it added that "the rise may be slower than forecast since, in addition to demand, supply has strengthened and the price trend has been mixed between paper grades this year".
"Wood products exports will rise five percent and paper and pulp exports almost seven percent next year," it said.
This would up the forest industry's demand for wood by some seven percent after a five percent average fall this year and logging prices would rise "somewhat".
It expected forest industry capacity utilisation to grow only little from this year's average level of 85 percent due to increased capacity.
A major factor of uncertainty was also the amount of supply coming to Europe from North American producers, METLA analyst Jari Kuuluvainen told Reuters.

In addition to making these own forecasts, METLA also surveyed the forest industry and forest owners on their outlook and Kuuluvainen said this time the two reports showed surprisingly similar expectations.
"The forest industry's expectations are in the same way cautiously optimistic as we are," METLA's Jari Kuuluvainen said.
"Apart from the paper industry, most respondents were of the opinion that an upturn has already happened," METLA said in its statement.
